Planets Tokyo - Enter a Changing Art World\",\"recommendText\":\"477.6k watching\"},\"hotScore\":\"7.4\",\"introduction\":\"TeamLab Planets TOKYO is an immersive digital art attraction created by art collective teamLab where visitors \\\"step into water.\\\" Here, you take off your shoes, roll up your pants, and walk barefoot through water, strolling among flowers and light. The artworks are generated in real-time by algorithms and continuously transform in response to your movements and those around you, subtly blurring the boundaries between people, artworks, and others. This venue once set the Guinness World Record for annual attendance by a single art group's attraction and has twice been awarded \\\"Asia's leading tourist attraction\\\" at the World Travel Awards.\\nWater-themed spaces are the signature here. \\\"The infinite water surface depicted by dancing koi and people\\\" allows you to step into water approx. knee-deep, where countless koi swim across the endlessly extending surface, transforming into scattered flowers upon contact and blooming flora that changes with the seasons. In the \\\"Boundless crystal universe,\\\" strings of light sculptures stretch infinitely in all directions, letting you use your phone to cast stars into the space and personally shape this sea of stars. The garden area's \\\"Floating garden\\\" fills the entire space with soil-free orchids growing in midair, where flowers rise as you walk and their fragrance subtly shifts with the time of day.\\nThe \\\"Sports forest\\\" zone transforms the art museum into a three-dimensional playground: leap on glowing bouncing balls, climb colorful poles suspended in midair, step on balance stones that change with your movements, and explore the world with your body. The \\\"Capture and collect forest\\\" lets you use a mobile app to capture various extinct animals and compile your own illustrated guide. The \\\"Co-create! Future garden\\\" invites everyone to paint together, with finished airplanes and butterflies flying into the world in 3D—especially great for family-friendly fun.\\nExperience tips: Barefoot is required in water and garden areas. We recommend wearing pants or shorts with roll-up hems for convenience. Some areas have mirrored floors where pants are more practical than skirts. For 3D exploration areas like the sports forest, wear shoes suitable for activity.\\n△Carp swim across the boundless water surface. The tower has an observation deck at 350 m and another at 450 m. From the top, visitors can enjoy a 360-degree panoramic view of Tokyo, and on clear days the view can extend to distant mountain ranges. The Tembo Galleria at 450 m features a spiral glass walkway encircling the tower, including a section with a glass floor where you can look straight down at the ground below, as if floating in midair. After nightfall, the tower is alternately lit in two lighting modes, \\\"Iki\\\" and \\\"Miyabi\\\"—the former sky blue and the latter purple—adding an elegant charm to Tokyo's nightscape. The image of Tokyo Skytree also frequently appears in Japanese dramas and anime, becoming a symbolic marker of Tokyo's skyline in the minds of many. The area beneath the tower has been developed into the mixed-use commercial and entertainment district Skytree Town, combining shopping, dining, and entertainment, and the Sumida Aquarium is located within it. off at 18 golf courses with Mount Fuji views\",\"recommendText\":\"501.1k watching\"},\"hotScore\":\"8.7\",\"introduction\":\"Mount Fuji spans Shizuoka Prefecture and Yamanashi Prefecture. This mountain, revered by the Japanese as the \\\"sacred peak,\\\" has been dormant since its eruption in 1707 and remains a major symbol of Japan.\\nOf course, if you want to experience Mount Fuji and the surrounding natural scenery up close, the Fuji Five Lakes area at the foot of the mountain to the north is a great choice. Among these, the reflection of Mount Fuji in Lake Kawaguchi is a classic view well worth seeing, and the nearby Oshino Hakkai is also a famous sight. Heiwa Park to the southeast is an excellent spot for viewing Mount Fuji; on clear, cloudless days you can clearly see the conical peak of Mount Fuji, and in fall or winter you can also see snow on the summit, which is especially beautiful.\\nMount Fuji has 4 main climbing entrances, namely Fujinomiya entrance, Subashiri entrance, Gotemba entrance, and Fujiyoshida (Kawaguchiko) entrance, with the first 3 all located within Shizuoka Prefecture. The route from the foot to the summit is divided into 10 stages, each called a \\\"station,\\\" all equipped with rest areas for visitors, and most visitors take a bus from Kawaguchiko to the halfway point of the mountainMount Fuji fifth station, then start climbing the mountain from here.\\nUpon reaching the summit of Mount Fuji, you can see the beautiful crater lake formed by the volcano, surrounded by eight peaks. As you tour around the crater, there is a weather station—the highest point in Japan—where you may want to take a commemorative photo. There is also a post office at the summit where you can send a postcard to family and friends. Additionally, watching the sunrise from Mount Fuji will be an unforgettable and wonderful experience.\\nIn addition to Mount Fuji itself, the scenery around its base is also very beautiful. At the northern foot are caves left by volcanic eruptions, in all kinds of shapes, some of which continuously emit steam.
